# 2024 CRESCENDO – hindsight

Source: user hindsight notes, batch 1 (2026-09-27).

## Game play / meta
- The meta evolved into **full-court passers plus one clean-up robot** that does the AMP and shoots into the SPEAKER.
  When the SPEAKER was amplified ("hot"), one of the passers usually came in to shoot one NOTE, to guarantee 4 shots
  into the amplified SPEAKER.
- One passer focused on ground pickup and passing from the allowed zone; the other focused on **stealing the other
  alliance's passes**, and joined the first passer when there was nothing to steal.
- Even so, the **alliance that won played a "traditional" cycling game**: two cyclists doing both AMP and SPEAKER,
  plus one defender. It had a great defender driver, and the captain drove with great stealing awareness. In some
  memorable (not frequent) moments it even stole and passed to itself to collect later, when there was more than
  one NOTE to steal.
- Elite shooters shot from everywhere: far, adjacent to the SPEAKER, from the safe zone near the AMP, and also did
  the AMP.
- **The TRAP was a trap**: some teams did it and gained points, but it was not required to be elite and added robot
  complexity. HARMONY and solo climbs happened at DCMP / Championship level.
- Because of AUTO collisions in the battle for the centre NOTES, most intakes were **under the bumper** (a few very
  good robots had an extended over-the-bumper intake).

## Dominant robots
- **1690** – very zippy, low-CoG, high-acceleration robot. Under-the-bumper intake into a low-pivot shooter arm
  ("a pizza box on a pivot") shooting with up/down rollers from varied distances. Also did the AMP, with advanced
  software that timed and synced the pivot motion with a slow shot to create the arc into the AMP (the author's
  team copied this robot but did not reach the same AMP accuracy). Shoots and collects in the same direction.
- **2056, 6329, 3467** – considered a simple and very effective solution: under-the-bumper intake into a high-pivot
  single-joint shooter arm that could aim and shoot from varied distances or "hammer" the NOTE down into the AMP.
  Collect and shoot on opposite sides; AMP on the same side as the intake.
- **9483, 1778** – over-the-bumper wide ground intake with effective shooting, including from long range; collect
  and shoot in opposite directions.
- **254, 987, 2910** – under-the-bumper intake into a turret shooter. 254 and 987 had a separate mechanism for the
  AMP/TRAP: 254's intake hands off to the shooter, which ejects/hands off to two rollers on an elevator that rise and
  eject into the AMP/TRAP; 987 had a similar idea on a low-pivot arm that routes the NOTE either to the shooter or to
  the AMP arm. 2910 had a deflector into the AMP but focused more on shooting/passing.
- **1678, 111, 125, 1706, 5460** – tilted fixed elevator with an adjustable-angle shooter; could shoot or do the AMP,
  and also did the TRAP.
- **6328, 3005, 33** – a more complex version of 1690 with a dedicated AMP extension: shoot like 1690, or raise the
  arm (higher than 1690's) with deflection rollers that route/bend the NOTE into the AMP.
- **9496** – very simple robot: under-the-bumper intake + fixed hooded shooter; excelled at the SPEAKER and passing.
  Intake and shoot in opposite directions.
- **4613** – like 9496, but with an adjustable shooter.

## Effective mechanisms
- **9483 / 1778 / 1678** over-the-bumper, wider ground intake routing NOTES into the shooter. 9483's intake could
  also hold the NOTE and, when pivoted up, eject it upward so it falls into the AMP.
- **1690 arm shooter** – low-CoG "pizza box" pivoting shooter.
- **1690 / 6328 / 2056** under-the-bumper intake – top roller and bottom kicker roller, plus left/right horizontal
  centering wheels (most teams used passive centering).
- **2056 shooter** – two sets of top/bottom wheels, left and right at different speeds to spin the NOTE.
- **1678 shooter** – like 2056 but with only one side set of wheels, for even more spin and a lighter mechanism.
- **2910 / 1778 AMP deflector** – shoot into a passive pole that deflects the NOTE into the AMP.
- **254 / 2910 turret** (complex).
